{{ElectionsOH}}

The '''2006 Ohio Attorney General election''' was held on November 7, 2006, to elect the [[Ohio Attorney General]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state senator and attorney [[Marc Dann]] defeated [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Ohio State Auditor|State Auditor]] and former attorney general [[Betty Montgomery]] with 52.61% of the vote in what was considered an [[Upset (competition)|upset]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bischoff |first=Laura |date=July 24, 2025 |title=The rise, fall and return of Democrat Marc Dann |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/state/2025/07/24/former-ohio-attorney-general-marc-dann-rebuilt-his-career/84460292007/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=September 13, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}}</ref> The election was held concurrently with a [[2006 United States Senate election in Ohio|U.S. Senate election]], [[2006 Ohio gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]], and other statewide races. Primary elections were held on May 2, 2006.

Dann would go on to resign as attorney general on May 14, 2008, following the discovery of an [[extramarital affair]] and claims of [[sexual harassment]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Leckrone |first1=Jim |last2=Pierog |first2=Karen |last3=Walsh |first3=Eric |date=May 14, 2008 |title=Ohio attorney general resigns in wake of scandal |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/us-politics/ohio-attorney-general-resigns-in-wake-of-scandal-idUSN14180629/ |access-date=September 13, 2025 |website=Reuters}}</ref> Dean was succeeded by [[Nancy H. Rogers]] in late May 2008 after being appointed by Governor [[Ted Strickland]], but did not seek a full term in the following [[2008 Ohio Attorney General special election|special election]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jindra |first=Christine |date=May 28, 2008 |title=Dean of Ohio State law school Nancy Rogers to head Ohio attorney general's office |url=https://www.cleveland.com/openers/2008/05/_susan_tave_zelman_will.html |url-access=limited |access-date=September 13, 2025 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref>

== Republican primary ==
=== Nominee ===
* [[Betty Montgomery]], [[Ohio State Auditor]] (2003-2007) and former attorney general (1995-2003)
=== Defeated in primary ===
* [[Tim Grendell]], state senator from the [[Ohio's 18th senatorial district|18th]] district (2005-2011) and former state representative from the 98th district (2001-2005)
=== Withdrew ===
* Ron O'Brien, [[Franklin County, Ohio|Franklin County]] Prosecutor (1997-2021)<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Eder |first1=Steve |last2=Drew |first2=James |date=January 28, 2006 |title=O'Brien exits, leaving 2 in GOP attorney general race |url=https://www.toledoblade.com/news/state/2006/01/28/O-Brien-exits-leaving-2-in-GOP-attorney-general-race/stories/200601280034 |access-date=September 13, 2025 |website=Toledo Blade}}</ref>
